Here are a few ideas we’ve already talked through that can help you stay connected:

• Set up a regular “virtual coffee break”  
  – Keep it short (15–30 minutes) and informal  
  – Agree on a time that works for everyone so no one feels pressured  
  – Use a reliable, easy-to-access video tool  

• Establish a few simple ground rules  
  – No work talk (or keep it to a minimum)  
  – Keep the tone light and casual  
  – Encourage everyone to share so one person doesn’t dominate  

• Frame it as a team proposal, not a mandate  
  – Bring it up in your next meeting as “something we might try,” not “something we have to do”  
  – Ask for people’s ideas on timing, format or topics  

• Be flexible and iterate  
  – If attendance is low or people feel it’s too long/short, adjust the schedule  
  – Solicit feedback after a few sessions to make sure it’s meeting everyone’s needs  

These virtual coffee breaks can boost morale, recreate some of that “water-cooler” camaraderie, and give everyone a reason to pause and connect.

Here are a few things to keep in mind when you head into the store:

1. Playability and Comfort  
   • Neck profile – try different shapes (slim “C,” fat “U,” etc.) to see what feels best in your hand  
   • Fretboard radius and fret size – flatter radii tend to feel better for faster runs, rounder radii can feel nicer for chording  
   • Action and setup – the strings shouldn’t be so high that it’s hard to fret, nor so low that you get buzz

2. Pickups and Electronics  
   • Humbuckers vs. single-coils – humbuckers (like on a Les Paul) give you a thicker, higher-gain sound; single-coils (like on a Strat) are clearer and chimey  
   • Coil-splitting or coil-tapping – if you want both humbucker warmth and single-coil sparkle, look for a guitar with a coil-split feature  

3. Versatility and Tone  
   • Try it in alternate tunings (open D, drop D, etc.) to make sure it stays in tune and the strings feel good under your fingers  
   • If you’re into fingerpicking (e.g. “Blackbird”-style intros), check how the guitar responds acoustically as well as plugged in  

4. Build Quality and Fit  
   • Check for any fret-buzz, binding issues, or finish blemishes  
   • Make sure the weight and body contours work for your playing style (standing vs. sitting)  

5. Your Musical Goals  
   • Think about the styles you play most—rock, blues, country, pop—and make sure the guitar’s voice matches  
   • If you want maximum tonal options, a Les Paul with coil-tap or a Strat-style guitar with varied pickup configurations can give you more flexibility  

Take your time, play through clean and overdriven amps, and bring along any accessories you normally use (capo, pedals, etc.) so you can really judge how it will perform for you. Have fun at the store!

Here are a few ideas building on what we’ve already discussed:

1. Lentil Bolognese bowls  
   • Make the simple lentil-tomato sauce you liked, then serve it over quinoa and toss in your favorite roasted veggies.  
   
2. Roasted Sweet Potato & Chickpea Bowls  
   • Cube sweet potatoes, toss with olive oil, chopped rosemary, garlic powder, salt and pepper, then roast until tender.  
   • Add a can of drained chickpeas (tossed in a little cumin and paprika) and finish with a squeeze of lemon or lime.  

3. Homemade Granola for Snacking or Topping  
   • Start with oats, nuts/seeds, a sweetener (honey or maple syrup) and oil, then customize with cinnamon, dried fruit, shredded coconut or chocolate chips.  

4. Double-Fried Sweet Potato Fries + Dipping Sauces  
   • Fry once at a lower temp (~325°F), let cool, then fry again at ~375°F for a crisp exterior and fluffy inside.  
   • Try a spicy mayo (mayo + sriracha + lime) or a chipotle-ranch (ranch + adobo sauce).  

5. Chicken Fajita Meal-Prep Bowls  
   • Slice chicken breast thinly, marinate in lime juice, chili powder, cumin, garlic and a touch of oil, then sauté with peppers and onions.  
   • Pack over rice or quinoa with salsa, avocado or a dollop of Greek yogurt.  

Mix and match any of the above for a week’s worth of balanced, protein-packed meals!
